abstract: As generative AI tools increasingly serve as news sources, understanding how users form trust in AI-generated news becomes critical. This study investigates the cognitive and social mechanisms underlying trust in AI news across three countries – the United States, Spain, and Chile – using a two-wave panel survey. Drawing on the HAII-TIME model (an adaptation of the Theory of InteractiveMedia Effects (TIME) for the Study of Human – AI Interaction (HAII)), we examine the role of the AI heuristic (perceiving AI as objective and unbiased) and the perception of AI as a social entity. Results show that AI news use and trust in AI news are relatively low. AI news use predicts increased trust over time. Longitudinal analyses reveal two distinct pathways consistent with mediation: the cue route via the AI heuristic and the action route via perceiving AI as a social entity, though the social entity path was more consistently supported across countries and measurement of AI news use (user vs. non-user or ordinal). The differences between measures support the claim that the cue route is triggered by identifying AI as source, whereas the action route is influenced by (frequency of) actual interactions. The differences between countries could be due to differences in culture and media systems.

ur.ai_reason: AI新闻信任为核心议题，两波面板调查用户信任机制
ur.tldr: 研究通过美国、西班牙、智利三国两波面板调查，探究用户对AI生成新闻的信任机制。发现AI新闻使用与信任度均较低，但使用频率能预测信任增长。基于HAII-TIME模型揭示两条路径：线索路径（AI启发式/客观性感知）和社会实体路径（AI社交性感知），后者跨文化一致性更强。实际互动频率影响路径差异，文化与媒体系统差异或可解释国家间分歧。

title: Cue and action routes to trust in AI news: results from a two-wave cross-cultural panel study
title_zh: 线索与行动路径对AI新闻信任的影响：一项两波跨文化面板研究
